title: Shorthand properties and computed property names
hook: When the property name matches the variable name, write { name } instead of { name: name }. When the key is dynamic, wrap it in brackets — essential for maps keyed by id and reducer action types.

blocks.text: **Property shorthand** `{ name, age }` is sugar for `{ name: name, age: age }` when keys match binding names. **Method shorthand** `{ greet() {} }` omits `: function`. **Computed property names** `[expression]` evaluate at object creation — `{ [prefix + 'Id']: value }`. **Symbol keys** can be computed too. Together they power Redux actions `{ type: SET_USER, payload }` and dynamic form field maps.

entries.plainDefinition: Omit : value when key name equals variable name.
Key from expression in brackets at runtime.
Method definition without function keyword in object literal.
Key not known until runtime — Map alternative for frequent add/remove.
entries.example: cache[userId] = session; // same as { [userId]: session } in literal

blocks.text: Reduces noise in factory returns and React setState object merges. Computed keys enable **table-driven code** — one reducer handles many field names. C# **anonymous types** require fixed property names at compile time; JS dynamic keys are native. Confusing computed key with shorthand when variable holds key name is a common bug.

blocks.title: Interview trap: shorthand vs computed
blocks.body: const k = 'id'; { k } creates property k (shorthand). { [k]: 1 } creates property id (computed). Different keys.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Using { field } when you meant { [field]: value }. Duplicate computed keys — last wins silently. Method shorthand losing this binding when destructured and passed unbound.

blocks.text: Prefer **Map** when keys are dynamic and non-string or frequent add/delete. Object literal computed keys allocate new object — fine for reducers. **Template literals** in keys: `{ [`user:${id}`]: profile }`. For TS, use Record<string, T> or mapped types when keys are finite union.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Cannot explain { k } vs { [k]: 1 }. Saying C# anonymous objects support computed keys. Unaware last duplicate key wins in object literal.

interviewTakeaways: Shorthand: { name } when key equals variable name.
Computed: { [expr]: value } when key comes from expression.
60s: Shorthand reduces noise. Brackets for dynamic keys. Method shorthand in literals. C# uses Dictionary for dynamic keys. Redux SET_FIELD pattern.
Follow-up: build object from array of [key,value] pairs with reduce.
commonPitfalls: Shorthand when computed key was intended for dynamic field name.
Destructuring method shorthand losing this when passed as callback.
